concept: Time series bucketing parameters: granularity, bucketMaxSpanSeconds, bucketRoundingSeconds
summary: Source-anchored research for Time series bucketing parameters: granularity, bucketMaxSpanSeconds, bucketRoundingSeconds. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: In MongoDB 7.1 and later, fixed-bucket query optimizations require a collection created with both custom parameters and no later parameter changes. For eligible predicates using $gte and $lt on the timeField, MongoDB can omit the per-measurement event filter when the query bounds align with bucket boundaries. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

The time-span setting is only one bucket constraint. MongoDB documents a maximum of 1,000 measurements or 125 KB per bucket, whichever is lower, so a configured maximum time span does not guarantee that a bucket remains open for that entire interval. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

During insertion, the BucketCatalog closes an open bucket if the incoming measurement would make the time between the bucket's oldest and newest timestamps exceed the collection's allowed span. A bucket closed for this reason remains eligible for reopening. bucketRoundingSeconds positions a new bucket's lower time boundary; it is not the span limit. (high confidence)

After collection creation, collMod can increase granularity or the custom span and rounding values but cannot decrease them. Existing bucket documents are not rewritten when the setting changes; the new span applies to new buckets. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

An October 2023 forum report describes MongoDB 7.0.2 rejecting a 300-second custom pair after an upgrade from 6.0.3 with the error that bucketMaxSpanSeconds was not configurable away from the default 3,600 for the provided granularity. A MongoDB respondent attributed the failure to an incomplete upgrade and advised following the release procedure; this is version-specific troubleshooting evidence. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-10-09)

MongoDB 6.3 and later supports manual fixed-window bucketing with bucketMaxSpanSeconds and bucketRoundingSeconds instead of granularity. The two values must be equal, between 1 and 31,536,000 seconds inclusive, and granularity must be omitted. bucketMaxSpanSeconds limits the oldest-to-newest time range in a bucket. When a new bucket is opened, bucketRoundingSeconds rounds the first measurement's timestamp down to determine the bucket's minimum time. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

MongoDB describes granularity as the expected cadence between measurements. Its presets map to bucketRoundingSeconds and bucketMaxSpanSeconds as follows: seconds = 60 and 3,600; minutes = 3,600 and 86,400; hours = 86,400 and 2,592,000. (high confidence)

In a September 2024 migration discussion, one user reported that custom 3,600-second bucketing made queries slower and the collection larger than using granularity: hours. This is a workload-specific report, not a general benchmark or a contradiction of the fixed-boundary rules. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-09-04)
